title: Elon Musk’s Austin home targeted by well-funded leftist groups aboard party buses
excerpt:
Fox News host Greg Gutfeld and the ‘Gutfeld!’ panel discuss Hillary Clinton saying she wants to force Elon Musk to testify to Congress if President Donald Trump pardons him.

Three far-left nonprofits...
body_text:
Fox News host Greg Gutfeld and the ‘Gutfeld!’ panel discuss Hillary Clinton saying she wants to force Elon Musk to testify to Congress if President Donald Trump pardons him.

Three far-left nonprofits with combined annual revenues of $56.1 million escalated their protests against SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk this week by targeting his Austin-area home with a seemingly innocuous post-election "party" featuring two chartered buses, music, speeches, theatrical Cybertruck piñatas and dancing to Queen’s "We Will Rock You."

The event’s organizers – VOCAL-TX, the fiscally-sponsored project of a New York 501(c)(3) nonprofit; the Center for Popular Democracy Inc., a 501(c)(3) nonprofit based in Brooklyn; and People’s Action, a 501(c)(4) political nonprofit based in Chicago – framed the Saturday event as a tame "People Over Billionaires Election After Party."

The demonstration reflected growing coordination among leftist networks worldwide, from Paris to Portland, Ore., supplying organizers, transportation, coalition partners, event platforms, messaging and other logistical support for actions presented as "grassroots." As Democratic politicians threaten investigations into Trump’s corporate backers, including Musk, the street protests help create the appearance of bottom-up support.

The leaders of the organizations behind the "After Party," held in West Lake Hills, Tex., where Musk owns a sprawling home, didn’t provide comment in response to queries from Fox News Digital, but they have insisted in the past that their local protests are the result of "organic" organizing in communities.

A now-ubiquitous, mass-produced anti-Musk "I AM STEALING FROM YOU" poster, featuring the tech billionaire with creepy eyes, has appeared at demonstrations nationwide and was also on display at the Austin protest outside his home.

At a May Day protest in Washington, D.C., on May 1, 2025, blocks from the White House, a protester from the communist Party for Socialism and Liberation carries a mass-produced poster created by a Democratic nonprofit to vilify Tesla CEO Elon Musk. (Asra Q. Nomani)

WHO’S FUNDING AMERICA’S PROTEST UNREST? FOX NATION'S NEW 'RIOT INC.' FOLLOWS THE MONEY TO FIND OUT

This weekend’s organizers helped lead the "Tesla Takedown" protests that sometimes turned ugly last year. According to a Fox News Digital investigation, 258 organizations with combined annual revenues of an estimated $2.6 billion were behind those protests.

At Saturday’s event, participants arrived at the property in two blue Fly-Rides party buses and additional vehicles. Organizers blasted music including Queen’s "We Will Rock You," over loudspeakers.

"We'll bring the music, you bring the dance moves! This is family friendly, peaceful and FUN event!" the organizers wrote, promoting the event.

The Austin American-Statesman covered the event and cast it playfully, with the headline "Dozens party outside Elon Musk's West Lake Hills home after campaign donations fell flat." It wrote about how organizers led a "Love Train" conga line and distributed party hats and refreshments, including cider.

The organizations behind the campaign are veterans of the professional protest industry. While this event was peaceful, the rhetoric of demonization and polarization at protests causes researchers at organizations like the Network Contagion Research Institute to conclude that that they can create a "permission structure" for political violence.

Last week, Musk blamed the issue on the U.S. military. (Getty Images)

‘ASTROTURF’: CRITICS SPECULATE TESLA PROTESTS ARE NOT A GRASSROOTS MOVEMENT, BUT A CAREFULLY ORGANIZED CAMPAIGN

The three nonprofits behind this weekend’s protests are part of a powerful national tax-exempt nonprofit industry that has increasingly taken to the streets over the past decade in coordinated, orchestrated campaigns in local communities, creating the image of homegrown organic demonstrations.

The three groups reported $56.1 million in combined 2024 revenue, according to their most recent tax filings.

Organizers promoted the event as a peaceful celebration of voters rejecting the influence of wealthy donors. About 60 people attended, according to estimates.

The demonstration followed in the spirit of the very coordinated "Tesla Takedown" protests launched at Texas dealerships in early 2025, when activists organized demonstrations against Tesla and Musk over his political activities and role in the new Trump administration and the Department of Government Efficiency, called DOGE. Those protests led to vandalism against Tesla vehicles and dealerships. A wider network of openly pro-communist groups, including Freedom Road Socialist Organization, carried posters with messages like "DOWN WITH BILLIONAIRES. WE NEED SOCIALISM."

Congressional lawmakers and Justice Department prosecutors are investigating an American-born, Shanghai-based tycoon, Neville Roy Singham, for funding and backing pro-communist groups. Some of those groups, including the Party for Socialism and Liberation, ANSWER Coalition, CodePink and People's Forum, have supported the regular protests that have hit America's streets, including the anti-Musk demonstrations.

On May 1, 2025, members of the Freedom Road Socialist Organization protested in Washington, D.C., blocks from the White House to support labor rights. "DOWN WITH BILLIONAIRES," a sign read, with an image of Elon Musk. "WE NEED SOCIALISM." (Asra Q. Nomani)

DEMOCRATS SET SIGHTS ON ELON MUSK PROBE AFTER MIDTERM WINS, BUT PRITZKER DRAWS A SURPRISING LINE

Much like the networks behind "No Kings," "Hands Off," "ICE Out" and other protests over the past year, the financial filings of the organizations behind this weekend’s demonstration show the scale of the infrastructure behind these groups.

The Center for Popular Democracy reported $40.9 million in 2024 revenue. People’s Action Institute reported $2.1 million, and Voices of Community Activists and Leaders Inc., or VOCAL-NY, which fiscally sponsors VOCAL-TX, reported $13.1 million. The organizations are separate entities, and the figures don’t represent a shared operating budget.

VOCAL-TX’s donation page identifies VOCAL-NY as its 501(c)(3) fiscal sponsor and sister organization. VOCAL-NY describes the organization as a statewide grassroots membership group focused on "building the power of low-income people" impacted by "HIV/AIDS, drug policy, mass incarceration, the war on drugs and homelessness." It says its work is "accomplished through community organizing, campaigns & harm reduction services."

The Center for Popular Democracy Inc. lists VOCAL-TX among its affiliates and describes itself as a network of "grassroots" organizations operating across dozens of states, building a "representative, multiracial society and government where all thrive, no exceptions," according to its nonprofit mission statement.

The protesters’ goal, according to the organization's website, is to send a crystal clear message that they are against Tesla CEO Elon Musk, describing itself as a decentralized grassroots movement that will "protest Tesla for as long as Elon Musk continues to shred public services." Organizers plan to hold rallies at over 200 Tesla location across the U.S. (Getty Images)

SOCIALIST, COMMUNIST GROUPS COORDINATE, PROMOTE 'SPONTANEOUS' ANTI-ICE PROTESTS IN AUSTIN

The Center for Popular Democracy reported $38.2 million in contributions and $14.6 million in other salaries and compensation in 2024. Its two co-executive directors received an average total compensation of $234,026, including bonuses in 2024, according to their latest tax filings, about four times more than the $63,360 median annual earnings of full-time, year-round U.S. workers that year.

VOCAL-NY reported nearly $3.5 million in other salaries and wages and listed its Texas co-director among its highest-paid employees, earning $113,842 in salary and $21,854 in bonuses in 2024.

People’s Action describes itself as a national network of grassroots groups "organized to promote economic, racial and social equity through national, regional and local advocacy campaigns."

Saturday’s gathering transformed a political victory "party" into a theatrical public spectacle, using buses, coordinated messaging, music and symbolic props to deliver a broader message: that billionaire wealth shouldn’t determine the direction of American politics. Protesters didn't specifically address the millionaires and billionaires that funnel money to Democratic politicians such as George Soros, Reid Hoffman and Pierre Omidyar, to name just a few.

Participants carried signs reading "Texas is not for sale" and "Alright Texas! Now let’s tax Musk." Attendees also smashed star-shaped and piñatas shaped like a Tesla Cybertruck.

On March 22, 2025, at a "Tesla Takedown" protest in Tysons, Va., a protester carries a mass-produced poster created by a Democratic nonprofit to vilify Tesla CEO Elon Musk, as she shoots a water gun at vehicles passing by on Tyco Road outside a Tesla showroom. (Asra Q. Nomani)

CHAOS INC.: COMMUNISTS, ANTIFA, AGITATORS IN THE RED-GREEN ALLIANCE

Eli Cortez, a VOCAL-TX bus captain, told attendees that the event was intended to celebrate voters rejecting the political influence of billionaires, according to coverage by the Austin American-Statesman. Cortez didn’t respond to a request for comment.

The demonstration focused on Musk’s spending during the 2026 election cycle. A New York Times analysis placed Musk’s total disclosed political spending at approximately $474 million, while other analyses based more narrowly on Federal Election Commission filings put the figure at roughly $445 million. About $212 million supported Texas Republican Ken Paxton’s unsuccessful Senate campaign through allied political committees.

May Day Strong, another far-left coalition tagged in the social media promotion of the event, describes itself as a "constellation" of more than 600 labor and community organizations, many of them socialist and communist. Its stated demands include taxing the rich, opposing ICE, expanding "democracy" and organizing workers to "protest, refuse to comply, and take the economic actions" needed to oppose the Trump administration.

At a May Day protest in Washington, D.C., on May 1, 2025, blocks from the White House, protesters from the communist Party for Socialism and Liberation carry mass-produced posters created by a Democratic nonprofit to vilify Tesla CEO Elon Musk. (Asra Q. Nomani)

Austin protesters carried a trademark poster with a creepy image of Musk and the message, "I Am Stealing From You," now a mainstay at protests, not as a spontaneous grassroots creation but a strategic asset. The Progressive Change Institute, the 501(c)(3) sister organization of the Progressive Change Campaign Committee, has taken credit for commissioning the art early last year by Washington, D.C., political street artist Absurdly Well.

The graphic became part of the propaganda of the broader "Hands Off" protest network, which distributed thousands of copies of the poster. CNN, the Associated Press, the New York Times, Axios, TIME, Reuters, The Hill and MSNBC host Rachel Maddow have splashed photos of the poster in its coverage Progressive Change Campaign Committee's online member engagement director has said the merchandise was intended to serve an organizing purpose beyond fundraising, with the goal of making Elon Musk "a real liability for the administration."

The group now gives donors "5- or 10-pack of anti-Elon Musk rally posters" in exchange for donations: $135 for a five-pack, $250 for a $10-pack and $30 for a single poster.

At least two of the iconic posters landed in the "party" protest outside Musk's home, held overhead by demonstrators.

Asra Nomani is senior editor of investigations at Fox News Digital. She is a former reporter at the Wall Street Journal, where she covered stories related to money, politics and society. She is the author of "Woke Army: The Red-Green Alliance That Is Undermining America’s Freedom." She can be reached at asra.nomani@fox.com and on X at @asranomani.

The Center for Popular Democracy reported $38.2 million in contributions and $14.6 million in other salaries and compensation in 2024. Its two co-executive directors received an average total compensation of $234,026, including bonuses in 2024, according to their latest tax filings, about four times more than the $63,360 median annual earnings of full-time, year-round U.S. workers that year.

VOCAL-NY reported nearly $3.5 million in other salaries and wages and listed its Texas co-director among its highest-paid employees, earning $113,842 in salary and $21,854 in bonuses in 2024.

People’s Action describes itself as a national network of grassroots groups "organized to promote economic, racial and social equity through national, regional and local advocacy campaigns."

Saturday’s gathering transformed a political victory "party" into a theatrical public spectacle, using buses, coordinated messaging, music and symbolic props to deliver a broader message: that billionaire wealth shouldn’t determine the direction of American politics. Protesters didn't specifically address the millionaires and billionaires that funnel money to Democratic politicians such as George Soros, Reid Hoffman and Pierre Omidyar, to name just a few.

Participants carried signs reading "Texas is not for sale" and "Alright Texas! Now let’s tax Musk." Attendees also smashed star-shaped and piñatas shaped like a Tesla Cybertruck.

On March 22, 2025, at a "Tesla Takedown" protest in Tysons, Va., a protester carries a mass-produced poster created by a Democratic nonprofit to vilify Tesla CEO Elon Musk, as she shoots a water gun at vehicles passing by on Tyco Road outside a Tesla showroom. (Asra Q. Nomani)

CHAOS INC.: COMMUNISTS, ANTIFA, AGITATORS IN THE RED-GREEN ALLIANCE

Eli Cortez, a VOCAL-TX bus captain, told attendees that the event was intended to celebrate voters rejecting the political influence of billionaires, according to coverage by the Austin American-Statesman. Cortez didn’t respond to a request for comment.

The demonstration focused on Musk’s spending during the 2026 election cycle. A New York Times analysis placed Musk’s total disclosed political spending at approximately $474 million, while other analyses based more narrowly on Federal Election Commission filings put the figure at roughly $445 million. About $212 million supported Texas Republican Ken Paxton’s unsuccessful Senate campaign through allied political committees.

May Day Strong, another far-left coalition tagged in the social media promotion of the event, describes itself as a "constellation" of more than 600 labor and community organizations, many of them socialist and communist. Its stated demands include taxing the rich, opposing ICE, expanding "democracy" and organizing workers to "protest, refuse to comply, and take the economic actions" needed to oppose the Trump administration.

At a May Day protest in Washington, D.C., on May 1, 2025, blocks from the White House, protesters from the communist Party for Socialism and Liberation carry mass-produced posters created by a Democratic nonprofit to vilify Tesla CEO Elon Musk. (Asra Q. Nomani)

Austin protesters carried a trademark poster with a creepy image of Musk and the message, "I Am Stealing From You," now a mainstay at protests, not as a spontaneous grassroots creation but a strategic asset. The Progressive Change Institute, the 501(c)(3) sister organization of the Progressive Change Campaign Committee, has taken credit for commissioning the art early last year by Washington, D.C., political street artist Absurdly Well.

The graphic became part of the propaganda of the broader "Hands Off" protest network, which distributed thousands of copies of the poster. CNN, the Associated Press, the New York Times, Axios, TIME, Reuters, The Hill and MSNBC host Rachel Maddow have splashed photos of the poster in its coverage Progressive Change Campaign Committee's online member engagement director has said the merchandise was intended to serve an organizing purpose beyond fundraising, with the goal of making Elon Musk "a real liability for the administration."

The group now gives donors "5- or 10-pack of anti-Elon Musk rally posters" in exchange for donations: $135 for a five-pack, $250 for a $10-pack and $30 for a single poster.

At least two of the iconic posters landed in the "party" protest outside Musk's home, held overhead by demonstrators.

title: GPs to offer 300,000 patients extra support to ease winter strain on NHS
excerpt:
£40m scheme in England aims to keep most vulnerable people well at home and avoid unnecessary hospital stays

Hundreds of thousands of vulnerable patients in England are to receive extra support from ...
body_text:
£40m scheme in England aims to keep most vulnerable people well at home and avoid unnecessary hospital stays

Hundreds of thousands of vulnerable patients in England are to receive extra support from their GP as part of a £40m drive aimed at keeping them out of hospital this winter.

As the NHS gears up for the pressures of the coming months, family doctors will offer 300,000 people with frailty and long-term conditions health checks, medication reviews and respiratory tests designed to prevent avoidable hospital admissions.

Funded by cash reallocated from existing GP budgets for 2026-27, the scheme will allow surgeries to identify and provide extra care to the patients they believe are most at risk of becoming seriously unwell in the winter. Groups of GP practices can use £126 for every eligible patient supported.

The prime minister said the scheme would be targeted at patients with heart disease, frailty and lung conditions such as emphysema and other types of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).

Andy Burnham said he was “not going to pretend this winter will be easy” but the programme would help keep people well at home and avoid unnecessary trips to hospital.

“If we want to take the pressure off our hospitals this winter, we’ve got to keep people well at home. So we’re backing GPs to reach the most vulnerable people early, before a small problem turns into a trip to A&E,” he said.

“People deserve the right care in the right place. And our NHS staff, who work so hard, deserve the right tools to provide it. I’m not going to pretend this winter will be easy. But with new technology, upgrades for hospitals and more care available closer to home, we’ll make sure the NHS is there for everyone when they need it.”

The health secretary, Yvette Cooper, said the scheme had been designed to offer greater support to the frailest patients.

“After such a heavy summer for our NHS as a result of the heat, everyone is working together to prepare for more challenging winter pressures,” she said. “That includes the rollout of flu vaccinations, investing in extra urgent care capacity and strengthening partnerships with social care.

“With thousands more GPs in post and millions more GP appointments this year, the £40m programme to support vulnerable patients in the community is part of our plan to help patients, improve primary care and also to support our NHS through the heavier winter months.”

Prof Victoria Tzortziou Brown, the president of the Royal College of GPs, said she welcomed the focus on prevention and supporting patients at greatest risk of avoidable hospital admission this winter.

“GPs’ clinical expertise, knowledge of their patients and continuity of care are central to identifying those most in need and providing personalised, coordinated support,” she said.

But she also said short-term initiatives alone could not deliver “sustained improvements in care” that patients with complex health needs required. Instead, she said, a longer-term approach to prevention was necessary, which must be backed by “sustainable investment in general practice”.

title: President Milei welcomes Pope Leo during historic visit to Argentina
excerpt:
Argentinian President Javier Milei has welcomed the head of the Catholic Church, Pope Leo XIV, upon his arrival at Jorge Newbery airport near Buenos Aires.

Milei and his sister, presidential secretar...
body_text:
Argentinian President Javier Milei has welcomed the head of the Catholic Church, Pope Leo XIV, upon his arrival at Jorge Newbery airport near Buenos Aires.

Milei and his sister, presidential secretary Karina Milei, greeted the pope on Sunday amid tensions between the government and Argentina’s Catholic Church over austerity measures.

Prior to his arrival, the pope spent three days in Uruguay, the first stop on his tour of Latin America.

He is the first pontiff to visit Argentina in nearly four decades, since John Paul II’s trip in 1987.

“Without a doubt, it gives us great joy that this pope is visiting us,” said Jorge Silanes, religious director at the Pequeno Cottolengo Don Orione, a home for people with disabilities in the Buenos Aires province.

In Argentina, Pope Leo’s schedule includes attending a welcome ceremony at Plaza San Martin and a meeting with Milei at the Casa Rosada, the official presidential palace.

But the pontiff’s visit comes amid shrinking membership in the Catholic Church in Latin America, as well as a sometimes fractious relationship with politicians like Milei.

Catholics comprise the largest religious group in Latin America, with as many as 425 million people identifying with the church.

But their numbers have shrunk over the last decade. A Pew Research Center survey found that, in Argentina, the percentage of self-identifying Catholics slipped from 71 percent in the 2013-2014 year to 58 percent a decade later.

Milei himself has suggested he considered converting to Judaism, though he was raised in the Catholic faith.

The Catholic Church has also criticised Milei’s austerity measures, which included slashing social spending and safety-net programmes for the poor.

Milei has defended the budget cuts as necessary to bring inflation under control.

Some members of the Catholic clergy, however, have taken a visible role in the protests against Milei’s measures.

Leo, 71, the first US-born pope, will remain in Argentina until Wednesday and meet with officials, diplomats and civil society representatives.

He will also visit a prison and celebrate mass in Buenos Aires, Lujan, and the province of Cordoba, before travelling to Peru, where he spent years serving as a bishop.

The previous pope, Francis, was born in Buenos Aires in 1936 and was the first pope from the Americas, but he never visited his home country as head of the Catholic Church. Francis died in 2025.

He and Milei had a notably contentious relationship, with the Argentinian president calling the late pontiff a “communist” and an “imbecile who defends social justice”.

“Leo is going to make the visit that Francis never did,” said Reverend Lorenzo “Toto” de Vedia, who works with poor communities in a neighbourhood of Buenos Aires.

title: US chipmaker Nvidia investigates CEO Jensen Huang over affair
excerpt: United States-based chipmaker Nvidia is investigating its chief executive officer, billionaire Jensen Huang, after he confirmed he had an intimate relationship with a woman accused of working for Chin...
body_text:
United States-based chipmaker Nvidia is investigating its chief executive officer, billionaire Jensen Huang, after he confirmed he had an intimate relationship with a woman accused of working for Chinese intelligence.

In an announcement on Sunday, Nvidia said the probe would be conducted by a “committee of independent directors” with outside counsel.

“While the board has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, the board’s inquiry will examine all available information,” Nvidia’s board of directors said.

It said the board continued to have “confidence in Jensen and his leadership team”. Huang will continue to lead Nvidia during the probe.

The investigation follows a report in The New York Times last month that Jensen may have been the target of a Chinese espionage plot.

China and the US have been in competition to dominate key tech sectors like artificial intelligence (AI).

Amid the AI boom, Nvidia has seen demand for its chips and programming interfaces explode, resulting in the company being valued in the trillions of dollars.

For years, the US has sought to restrict the export of advanced chips to China, fearing the Asian superpower could gain an edge over its technology and military sectors.

But on October 29, The New York Times said it had obtained exclusive information that a Chinese woman named Alice Huang, or Huang Le, sought to cultivate close ties with Jensen Huang in an effort to glean information about Nvidia’s technology.

The Chinese Embassy in Washington, DC, has denied any allegations of spying in the case.

The New York Times also reported that Alice Huang’s employer, Megaspeed, had become one of Nvidia’s largest buyers, purchasing some $4.8bn in equipment from the US firm.

Jensen Huang’s ties to Alice Huang, who is of no relation, spurred fierce bipartisan backlash in the US Congress in the aftermath of the report.

“For months, bipartisan members of Congress have raised concerns about NVIDIA’s advanced AI chips going to China,” Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren wrote in a statement.

“NVIDIA’s Jensen Huang and NVIDIA’s board owe Congress answers. And we need to pass bipartisan legislation we have ready to stop advanced American technology from going to China.”

Republican lawmakers in the House of Representatives also called on Huang to appear and testify before Congress about the affair on November 18.

“It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which US national security has been placed at risk,” Republicans John Moolenaar, Brian Mast and Rick Crawford said in a statement.

In an email to Nvidia staff on Sunday, Huang had admitted to having an extramarital relationship.

“I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse ‌for what I did,” Huang said.

Nvidia has grown rapidly in recent years with the rise of AI, producing chips for large language models developed by companies like OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and Google.

Huang has also been closely working with US President Donald Trump since the Republican leader returned to office in 2025.

In August of that year, the Trump administration announced it would take a 15 percent cut of certain Nvidia chip sales to China.

Trump reportedly bought as much as $1.6m in Nvidia stock and sold about $1m in August, ahead of November’s midterm elections.

After the midterm races last Tuesday, stocks for AI-related companies, including Nvidia, tumbled in reaction to widespread Republican losses.

Trump has pushed back against calls to regulate AI companies, but many Democrats during the midterms campaigned on placing restrictions on the companies, including on the construction of data centres.

Nvidia lost $450bn in market value in a single trading day last week, but it rebounded on Friday, regaining 4 percent of its losses.

Joe Burrow of the Cincinnati Bengals celebrates a touchdown against the Baltimore Ravens during the third quarter in the game at M&T Bank Stadium on Nov. 27, 2025 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Patrick Smith/Getty Images)

Burrow threw three touchdown passes and ran for another touchdown in a convincing 34-17 victory over the Atlanta Falcons.

Burrow missed on only five passes while throwing for 271 yards. And that was more than solid. But context is everything and as this season goes, the context is much more impressive.

His passer rating is 132.0 in those four combined games.

"I loved putting on a show for the people of Spain and was happy to be here," Burrow said afterward in English.

The show in Spain is just one of 17 acts Burrow and the Bengals must perform this regular season and if one starts mathing what has happened with how that projects over a 17-game season, the MVP talk gets quite loud.

At his current eight-game pace, Burrow would project over 17 games to:

And, no, this is not a prediction of what is about to happen. The Bengals are about to find themselves in some very difficult matchups against the Pittsburgh Steelers, Kansas City Chiefs and probably the Carolina Panthers.

"We've just played together for so long now," Burrow said. "We're coming up on 10 years playing together. So, you know, when you do that, you develop that connection mentally that nothing needs to be said."

This needs to be said: The only thing we believe can contain Burrow and that Cincinnati offense is an injury to the quarterback.

We say this because that's what history has said unequivocally. That history is something Bengals fans hate to recall.

But it is there, including in two of the last three seasons.

You can open your eyes again, Who Dey, folks. None of this is meant to slime Burrow or predict something terrible.

It is, however, predicting that if Burrow can stay healthy, he's got that MVP award within reach. That's how it definitely sounded after Sunday's dismantling of the Falcons' defense.

title: Man charged with murder over fatal stabbing of HungryPanda delivery rider in Melbourne

Footscray man charged over death of 47-year-old Feng Jianming in the CBD on Friday night

A man has been charged with murder after a delive...
body_text:
Footscray man charged over death of 47-year-old Feng Jianming in the CBD on Friday night

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A man has been charged with murder after a delivery rider was stabbed to death while working, leaving his family bereft and a city in mourning.

On Friday night, HungryPanda delivery rider Feng Jianming, 47, and another rider confronted a man allegedly tampering with their bikes in Melbourne’s city centre.

An altercation ensued and the man, a 51-year-old, is alleged to have stabbed both riders.

Emergency services rushed to the scene on Frederick Way, but Feng could not be saved.

The second rider, 34, was taken to hospital with serious injuries, where he remained on Monday.

The 51-year-old was arrested by police on Saturday and on Monday morning was charged with one count of murder and intentionally causing serious injury.

Feng, originally from China’s Shaanxi Province, had been in Australia for about nine years.

His wife, Xu, their four parents and two children all relied on his hard work to get by at home.

The news of Feng’s death reverberated through Melbourne and gig worker communities in Australia and abroad.

Mourners left floral tributes and notes near the state library over the weekend in his memory.

Some cards expressed sympathy for his family, while others vented grave frustrations with messages such as “city of criminal” and “Asian lives matter”.

A GoFundMe fundraiser set up by the Melbourne Chinatown Business Association had raised almost $390,000 by Monday morning to help Feng’s family with emergency travel and funeral expenses.

Food delivery company HungryPanda said it was assisting the family with visa arrangements, funeral expenses, financial support and insurance.

The 51-year-old man was remanded in custody to appear before Melbourne magistrates court on Monday.

title: Why Trump wants UFC chief Dana White as his new White House press secretary
excerpt:
Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) chief executive Dana White is set to meet United States President Donald Trump on Monday to discuss taking the job of White House press secretary.

Trump announced...
body_text:
Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) chief executive Dana White is set to meet United States President Donald Trump on Monday to discuss taking the job of White House press secretary.

Trump announced the offer on Saturday, days after his Republican Party suffered record losses in midterm elections. In a post on Truth Social, the president praised White as “a violent Fighter and Warrior” who would bring along leading UFC fighters as “assistants” to “defend us against the Lunatic Left”.

But it remains unclear how serious the offer is. In a news conference on Saturday, White confirmed he would travel to Washington, DC, to meet with Trump. But he also signalled concerns about his existing workload.

“I got a lot of jobs already,” White, a Trump ally and donor, said. “We have a meeting on Monday, so I’m sure I’ll have more to talk about after that.”

White also posted a photo to Instagram Stories of himself standing behind the White House podium. Its caption read, “On to the next chapter.”

Trump, too, posted his own AI-generated memes about the potential hire.

On Sunday, he shared an animated cartoon of White in the White House briefing room, flanked by a row of fighters. One of them body-slams a reporter who asks, “Is Trump a threat to democracy?”

The press secretary role has been vacant since Katie Zacharia’s brief tenure ended ‌last ⁠month. She left the post within five days of being hired after facing criticism that she presented herself as a lawyer without being licensed in the US.

Zacharia succeeded Karoline Leavitt, who stepped down from the role at the end of August, citing the needs of her growing family.

But why is the head of a mixed martial arts franchise being considered for the new public face of the Trump administration? Al Jazeera explains that and more in this brief explainer.

A former bouncer and small-time boxer, White began his career as a businessman by opening a boxing gym in Boston where he trained other fighters.

He later moved to Las Vegas, where he continued to run gyms and manage emerging fighters.

The UFC was founded in 1993, at about the time White resettled in Las Vegas. The organisation sought to offer an arena for fighters from different disciplines – from boxing to wrestling to jujitsu – to face each other in “no-holds-barred” competition.

In 2001, White convinced two casino magnate friends to buy the UFC for $2m and name him president. Since then, he has built the company up through big fights and lucrative pay-per-view television deals.

He has been a fixture in the UFC in the more than two decades since. White has been credited with turning the fledgling franchise into a global business that brought mixed martial arts into the mainstream.

In 2016, the UFC was sold for $4bn, and in 2023, White became its CEO after a merger with World Wrestling Entertainment valued at some $21bn.

White has been a longtime supporter of Trump, appearing by his side at campaign events for nearly a decade.

Trump, in turn, has a history of hosting UFC fights as far back as 2001. At the time, UFC was struggling against criticism that the sport was too violent.

White had just taken up his position as UFC president, and he and Trump came to an agreement to host that year’s UFC championship at Trump’s Taj Mahal casino in Atlantic City, New Jersey.

The next year, the UFC returned to the Taj Mahal.

Speaking in support of Trump at the 2016 Republican National Convention, White recalled how the early collaboration helped open doors for the UFC, making other venues more accessible.

“No arenas wanted us,” White said at the time. “This guy reached out, and he’s always been a friend to me.”

The 2016 election cycle would mark Trump’s first successful bid for public office. In 2018, White was invited to visit the White House during Trump’s inaugural term as president.

During the 2020 elections, White again endorsed Trump as he sought a second term as president. White also donated $1m to Trump’s campaign and was a key speaker at the Republican Party’s national convention that year.

“I’ve known this man for 20 years. We’ve actually become even closer since he’s become the president of the United States,” White told supporters at a rally in Colorado. “He’s a fighter. He loves this country. He’s doing great things for this country, and we’ve got to win this election again.”

Trump lost the 2020 race to Democrat Joe Biden. But four years later, in 2024, he launched another re-election bid, and successfully won a second term.

During that campaign, Trump credited White with helping him connect with younger voters.

“He introduced me to people I never heard of, young kids,” Trump told Time Magazine in May. “I was being interviewed by 20-year-old kids. I’m saying, ‘Where the hell did you meet these people?’ They’re called influencers.”

Experts say Trump’s 2024 campaign benefitted significantly from his UFC connections.

Ahead of his victory, Trump courted influencers like UFC fan Theo Von and UFC host Joe Rogan, whose podcast boasts about 11 million listeners per episode.

Trump has also used his second term as president to elevate the UFC’s profile, weaving one of its events into plans to celebrate the 250th US Independence Day.

Dubbed “UFC Freedom 250”, the tournament was given unusual access to national monuments for a commercial event.

White, for instance, hosted a weigh-in for fighters on the steps of the Lincoln Memorial, with uniformed military personnel standing as an honour guard. The fights themselves were held on the lawn of the White House.

Trump called the event “one of the most exciting days in the history of our fabled White House”.

But critics warned the event could constitute a conflict of interest: In the months before the fight, Trump reportedly bought up to $50,000 of stock in TKO Holding, the UFC’s parent company.

A lawsuit also challenged the UFC’s use of public facilities, calling the event “deeply corrupt”.

Some opposition figures have dismissed Trump’s idea of appointing White as press secretary as a way to distract attention from the midterm elections.

During the November 3 elections, Trump’s Republican Party suffered record losses, losing majorities in both the House of Representatives and the Senate.

Melat Kiros, a Democrat elected to represent Colorado in the House, said on Saturday that Trump’s offer to White “demonstrates how deeply unserious this man is, how ridiculous this administration is”.

Democratic Senator Mark Kelly, meanwhile, said Trump’s choice raised questions about the president’s wellbeing.

“It would be really funny if it wasn’t dangerous, if he wasn’t the president,” Kelly said. “Countries around the world are continuing to laugh at us because of what he’s doing.”

There has also been some speculation that Trump may have tapped the wrong Dana White.

A woman by the same name formerly worked as a Pentagon spokesperson during Trump’s first term. She has denied being approached for the press secretary role.

“To everyone texting me congratulations: thank you, but you have the wrong Dana White,” she wrote on LinkedIn.

title: Chynna Phillips admits she considered calling lawyer to end Billy Baldwin marriage after 'treacherous times'
excerpt:

body_text:
The Wilson Phillips singer told Fox News Digital at Chiller Theatre Expo how close she came to ending her marriage and what convinced her to keep working on their relationship.

Chynna Phillips and Billy Baldwin's marriage has weathered some difficult moments, including a time when the singer considered ending their relationship.

Chynna Phillips and Billy Baldwin stand backstage. (FilmMagic)

"If we're being completely transparent here, there were times where I was just thinking to myself, I can't do this anymore."

WATCH: CHYNNA PHILLIPS OPENS UP ABOUT NEARLY ENDING MARRIAGE TO BILLY BALDWIN: 'TREACHEROUS TIMES'

Despite reaching that breaking point, Phillips said her husband's willingness to work on their relationship gave her hope that things could improve.

"But then when I saw that he was actually willing to work on the relationship in a very intentional way, the two of us were able to make some changes that were permanent," she said.

Phillips explained that the couple began making lasting changes rather than falling back into the same patterns after a brief period of improvement.

WILLIE ROBERTSON'S FAITH-BASED ADVICE THAT'S KEPT HIS 34-YEAR MARRIAGE TO WIFE KORIE STRONG

"We have been working very, very hard," she said.

Phillips and Baldwin tied the knot in September 1995 and share three adult children, Jameson, Vance and Brooke.

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

Their marriage has made headlines in recent years as the couple has spoken publicly about their decision to live separately at different points in their relationship.

In October, Phillips confirmed that she and Baldwin had moved into separate houses while continuing to work through their marital challenges.

"Literally our marriage was going down like the Titanic, and Billy moved 50 yards away from me in the guest house and so far, so good," Phillips said in an Instagram video.

"It's kind of working. I'm not really sure what's going to come of it but hey, I'm not fighting it."

A post shared by Chynna Phillips Baldwin (@chynna_phillips)

The couple previously lived apart in 2024, with Phillips staying in Santa Barbara and Baldwin living in Beverly Hills. They later reunited under one roof before deciding to live separately again.

Chynna Phillips and husband Billy Baldwin have been married for more than three decades. (Getty Images)

Now, Phillips and Baldwin are preparing to give fans a closer look at their relationship through a new YouTube series, "Holding On: Billy and Chynna," scheduled to debut Nov. 17.

During her interview with Fox News Digital, Phillips encouraged viewers to check out the project, which she said offers an unfiltered look at the realities of marriage.

"It really depicts marriage, the ups, the downs, it's very raw, it's very real, it is very funny, and it's super engaging in my opinion," she said. "I'm a little biased, but..."

MARCUS MUMFORD SAYS BIBLE CAMP SPARKED DECADES-LONG LOVE STORY WITH WIFE CAREY MULLIGAN

In a teaser shared on Instagram, Baldwin and Phillips were seen discussing some of the tensions in their relationship.

"You can't admit when you're wrong. That's just it," Baldwin told his wife in the preview.

In another clip, Baldwin said Phillips had told him she wanted to spend her life with him, but wanted to spend it "adjacent."

While Phillips has been candid about the challenges in her marriage, family remains an important part of her life.

WATCH: CHYNNA PHILLIPS SAYS BOND WITH FAMOUS SISTERS IS STRONGER THAN EVER: 'NOW WE'RE INSEPARABLE'

The singer also reflected on her evolving relationship with her sisters, Mackenzie and Bijou Phillips, during her conversation with Fox News Digital.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Stephen Baldwin, Bijou Phillips, Mackenzie Phillips, Chynna Phillips and Billy Baldwin attend the 2026 Chiller Theatre Halloween Expo at the Dolce Hotel on Oct. 30, 2026, in Parsippany, N.J. (Getty Images)

"It's interesting because we didn't grow up together," Phillips said.

"Bijou and Mackenzie spent a lot more time together than I did with them. I was basically raised as an only child, but as I matured and grew older, I reached out more to them, and we all started spending more time together and now we're inseparable."

Phillips, whose father was the late musician John Phillips of The Mamas & the Papas, said the sisters have developed a strong bond despite their different childhood experiences.

Chynna Phillips is the daughter of the late John Phillips, a founding member of The Mamas & the Papas. (Alamy Stock Photo)

"We spend a whole lot of time together, and we trust each other implicitly," she said.

"Of course, we've had our ups and our downs just like any siblings. But we really love one another and I think that we share, since we share the same father, there's just a very strong connection between us."

WATCH: Chynna Phillips embraces California roots and family life: 'I'm a California girl'

Faith has also played a significant role in Phillips' life, although she said she doesn't frequently discuss her beliefs with her sisters.

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

"I don't really talk about my faith too much with my sisters, but they know that I love the Lord," she said.

"So I just kind of pray for them, and I know that they're in the Jesus waiting room."

These days, Phillips said she enjoys a quieter lifestyle in Santa Barbara, where she spends time cooking, taking walks and relaxing at home.

With her three children now grown, she also finds joy in caring for her two dogs, Hula and Hoops.

"I just love being at home and cooking. And I love taking long naps and walks and hanging out with Billy," she said.

title: Video shows small plane clip pickup truck during emergency landing on busy Florida road
excerpt:
A small plane comes dangerously close to hitting a truck before touching down on a busy Florida roadway.

A small plane turned a Florida road into an emergency runway Saturday, crashing into the back ...
body_text:
A small plane comes dangerously close to hitting a truck before touching down on a busy Florida roadway.

A small plane turned a Florida road into an emergency runway Saturday, crashing into the back of a moving pickup truck in a dramatic close call captured on video.

Two pilots were aboard the aircraft when a mechanical issue forced them to attempt an emergency landing near Bayshore Road and Interstate 75 in North Fort Myers around noon, according to the Lee County Sheriff’s Office.

The plane departed Sebring, Florida, around 11 a.m. Saturday and made the emergency landing about 50 minutes later, at 11:50 a.m., according to FlightAware tracking data.

DASHCAM VIDEO CAPTURES SMALL PLANE CRASHING ON SAN JOSE HIGHWAY, INJURING THREE ON BOARD, INCLUDING CHILD

Responders assess the scene after a small plane struck a pickup truck while making an emergency landing on Bayshore Road. Authorities reported no injuries. (Lee County Sheriff's Office)

Video captured from the road shows the plane’s wheels touch down on the asphalt as it speeds along Bayshore Road, its wing clipping the rear of a pickup traveling in the same direction.

The truck was heading eastbound when the aircraft struck it, according to the sheriff’s office. No injuries were reported.

Images shared by the sheriff’s office show the aftermath, with the small aircraft sitting on the roadway.

"Thankfully, this incident had a positive outcome, and no one was injured," Lee County Sheriff Carmine Marceno said in a statement.

NTSB FINDS 'NO EVIDENCE' OF MAR-A-LAGO CONNECTION AFTER FLORIDA JET CRASH KILLS NINE PEOPLE

A Cessna marked N2905U sits partly on the grass beside Bayshore Road following an emergency landing in North Fort Myers, Florida. (Lee County Sheriff's Office)

"Given the recent tragic news involving aviation accidents, we are especially grateful that everyone is safe."

Marceno credited patrol deputies, FDOT Southwest Florida and Bayshore Fire Rescue for their quick response.

PILOTS' PUSH TO LEVEL JET MAY HAVE TORN OFF KEY PIECE FOUND MILES FROM FLORIDA CRASH, FORMER NTSB EXPERT SAYS

A small plane rests along Bayshore Road after striking a pickup truck during an emergency landing Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026. No injuries were reported. (Lee County Sheriff's Office)

"We will continue working closely with our partners at the FAA as they review the circumstances surrounding this incident," he said.

The Federal Aviation Administration is leading the investigation, according to the sheriff’s office.

PRIVATE JET WITH 9 PEOPLE ON BOARD CRASHES JUST MILES FROM MAR-A-LAGO

The close call came less than a week after a Learjet crashed Sunday, Nov. 1, in Greenacres in Palm Beach County, killing all nine people aboard.

Federal investigators are working to determine what caused that crash.

Stepheny Price is a Writer at Fox News with a focus on West Coast and Midwest news, missing persons, national and international crime stories, homicide cases, and border security.

title: Alligator attack on Florida mom sparks panicked 911 call: 'Her arm is gone'
excerpt: A nearly 12-foot alligator kills 71-year-old Steven Hamilton while he is fishing in Winter Garden, Florida. Reporter Madison Scarpino details how officials captured and killed the alligator. Local pol...
body_text:
A nearly 12-foot alligator kills 71-year-old Steven Hamilton while he is fishing in Winter Garden, Florida. Reporter Madison Scarpino details how officials captured and killed the alligator. Local police warn the public to respect wildlife and keep their distance after this second deadly alligator attack in the state this year.

Newly released 911 calls capture the frantic aftermath of an alligator attack that left a Florida woman with severe injuries, according to reports.

The attack occurred as Dina Spann, 58, was swimming with a group in Florida's Silver River near Ray Wayside Park in Marion County over the summer.

Spann survived the attack but lost her right arm below the elbow and part of a finger on her left hand.

FLORIDA DAD MAKES FINAL FACETIME CALL TO WIFE BEFORE DYING IN FLASH FLOOD

Audio of two 911 calls obtained by The New York Post captured the frantic moments after the attack, including witnesses describing Spann's severe injuries.

"Somebody got bit by an alligator, I think her arm got bit — it’s dangling off," one woman said in the call, the Post said. "She lost half an arm."

Dina Spann, 58, lost her right arm below the elbow and part of a finger on her left hand after an alligator attack in Florida. (Dina Spann via Facebook)

In another 911 call, a woman can be heard screaming and crying as a man tells the dispatcher they are on the Silver River.

"Her arm is gone," the second 911 caller said.

MOM OF 2 WHO DIED RESCUING SONS DURING BAHAMAS SNORKELING TRIP IS IDENTIFIED

Fox News Digital reported on the August incident earlier this year.

At the time, Spann's son, Zach Guerrina, told the Post his mother was trying to hold the alligator's jaws open so she could escape.

Witnesses described a chaotic scene after an alligator attacked Dina Spann, seen above, in a Florida river. (Dina Spann via Facebook)

"It had her, but she said she was trying to make sure it didn’t get to her legs," he said.

Other eyewitnesses shared their accounts of the incident.

CROCODILE ATTACK HORROR UNFOLDS AS COUPLE TRIES TO SAVE VICTIM: ‘WE FELT SO HELPLESS’

A park visitor named John Gamache told FOX 35 Orlando he saw an alligator's "head way above the water and going full speed" toward the swimmers.

Gamache then rushed toward the swimmers in his boat.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"It was a terrible injury, bones poking out, blood everywhere," Gamache said.

A woman lost her right arm after an alligator (not pictured) attacked her while she was swimming in a Florida river. (iStock)

Spann was transported to a hospital after the attack, and FOX 35 reported earlier this summer that she was in good spirits when she returned home.

Spann's family also called Gamache to thank him, as FOX 35 noted.

"They called earlier, and we talked for a while, and it was heartwarming to hear them explain their emotions," Gamache said.

Other alligator attacks have occurred in Florida this year.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Earlier this year, a child was hospitalized with non-life-threatening injuries after being bitten on the arm and leg by an alligator while swimming in an off-limits Florida nature preserve.

Florida is home to a large population of alligators, which are frequently found in the state's rivers, lakes, marshes and other freshwater habitats. (Anadolu via Getty Images)

In October, a 71-year-old man was killed by a nearly 12-foot alligator while fishing along the shore of Lake Apopka in Florida, marking the state's second fatal alligator attack of the year, according to police.

Fox News Digital's Kelly McGreal and Jessica Mekles contributed reporting.

Andrea Margolis is a lifestyle reporter for Fox News Digital and Fox Business. Readers can follow her on X at @andreamargs or send story tips to andrea.margolis@fox.com.

title: Week 10 AP Poll sees Georgia rightfully take over top spot while voters continue to award USC for no reason
excerpt: Tuesday night didn't just feature shocking results from the mid-terms, but shocking results in the first edition of the 2026 CFP Rankings, and Craig Carton can't believe they had Alabama ranked so hig...
body_text:
Tuesday night didn't just feature shocking results from the mid-terms, but shocking results in the first edition of the 2026 CFP Rankings, and Craig Carton can't believe they had Alabama ranked so high!

Week 10 had the potential to be one of the more chaotic and disruptive weekends of the college football season, with seven ranked-on-ranked matchups. Naturally, five of those seven matchups were won by the favorite, and instead of a weekend resulting in chaos, it was a weekend of teams making statements.

It's always the loaded slates that hardly ever meet expectations, and the weekends you least expect that deliver the goods.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

No team sent a stronger statement on Saturday than the Georgia Bulldogs with their 42-7 dismantling of Ole Miss on the road, and they were rewarded with the No. 1 being added next to their name. The Dawgs and Rebels each threw for 186 yards in the game, but all was not equal on the ground, as Georgia dominated both lines of scrimmage and picked up 295 rushing yards compared to Ole Miss' 66 yards on the ground.

Georgia Bulldogs wide receiver Talyn Taylor (1) celebrates after scoring a touchdown against the Mississippi Rebels during the second half at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images (Petre Thomas-Imagn Images)

Perhaps the biggest stunner from Week 10 is that AP voters finally got things right, at least for the most part.

Yes, they caught a break with the mostly chalk results and a lack of difficult decisions to make, but for as much as we love to pile it on when the poll is a disaster, we have to tip our cap on the rare occasion that the poll makes a lot of sense.

Georgia may have a loss, unlike the two unbeatens of Utah and UCLA, but there is no reality where someone could watch what the Bulldogs did to Ole Miss on Saturday night and not tab them as the No. 1 team in the country.

If anyone wants to waste energy arguing about how UCLA and Utah should both be ranked ahead of one-loss Notre Dame, they can have at it.

Just like there isn't a world where Georgia shouldn't be ranked No. 1, there also isn't a world where voters were going to put both Utah and UCLA ahead of the Fighting Irish after they knocked off Miami.

Notre Dame couldn't stay put at No. 4 after beating the team that the same voters had ranked No. 1 in the country one week ago. And no, it does not matter that Miami's best player, Malachi Toney, did not play.

ALABAMA FINALLY PUTS IT ALL TOGETHER, DOMINATES LSU AND LEAVES LANE KIFFIN STARING AT $40 MILLION CFP DISASTER

Notre Dame Fighting Irish cornerback Jayden Sanders (12) reacts after a play against the Miami Hurricanes during the second half at Notre Dame Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Michael Caterina-Imagn Images (Michael Caterina-Imagn Images)

Is Alabama being ranked No. 7 and Tennessee being ranked No. 9 that big of a deal? No, none of this is with the College Football Playoff Rankings taking all precedence, but Vols fans have every right to be frustrated with the Tide being ranked ahead of them.

Alabama and Tennessee are both 7-2 on the season, and with the Volunteers beating the Crimson Tide by 16 points earlier this season, the 'tiebreaker' should go Tennessee's way. On top of that, Tennessee dominated then No. 8 Kentucky 34-6 in Week 10.

NO 3 UTAH REMAINS UNDEFEATED WITH THRILLING WIN OVER NO 9 BYU BEHIND HEISMAN FINALIST DEVON DAMPIER'S EPIC DAY

Daune Morris #17 of the Tennessee Volunteers runs the ball for a touchdown during the NCAA football game between the University of Tennessee Volunteers and the University of Kentucky Wildcats at Neyland Stadium, Knoxville, TN Tim Gangloff/CSM/Sipa USA (Credit Image: Tim Gangloff/Cal Sport Media/Sipa USA) (Tim Gangloff/Cal Sport Media/Sipa USA)

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Alabama going to Baton Rouge and beating up on then No. 15 LSU on Saturday can't and shouldn't be ignored, but with Tennessee winning the head-to-head and having the more impressive win on paper, it doesn't make much sense to have the Vols ranked behind the Tide this week.

Tennessee fans can also point a (small) finger at Texas in this situation as well. The Longhorns beat Tennessee in Knoxville, hence their ranking ahead of the Vols, and with voters having to rank these teams somewhere, Texas really not being able to fall anywhere other than No. 8 adds another wrinkle to the mess.

If we got into all the resumes, hypotheticals, and head-to-head matchups, we'd be here all day.

We pointed out last week that the Trojans were getting way too much love from the voters, moving up to the No. 18 spot after knocking off what we now know is a very mediocre Ohio State team.

Head coach Lincoln Riley of the USC Trojans walks through the tunnel with his team prior to a game between the Ohio State Buckeyes and the USC Trojans at LA Memorial Coliseum on October 31, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Brenton Tse/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) (Brenton Tse/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images)

This week, USC was on a bye, and its signature win against the Buckeyes looks even worse with Ohio State losing to Oregon, yet the Trojans moved up three spots to No. 15 by simply not playing.

I'd say make it make sense, but it doesn't. USC has one notable win against a now three-loss Buckeyes team and losses to Oregon and Wisconsin. That is not the resume of a Top 15 team in the country.

Actual reality will fall into place in Week 11 when the Trojans travel to Bloomington to take on No. 6 Indiana in a monster matchup.

Mark Harris is a writer for OutKick. Follow him on X @itismarkharris.

title: Ring girl Sydney Thomas proves that the best way to pay tribute to someone is still by putting boobs on them
excerpt: "Pat McAfee never said not one time, 'Nobody can criticize me.' What Pat McAfee has said is, 'If you're going to criticize me to the point where the FBI tells me to wear Kevlar, then I'm going to crit...
body_text:
"Pat McAfee never said not one time, 'Nobody can criticize me.' What Pat McAfee has said is, 'If you're going to criticize me to the point where the FBI tells me to wear Kevlar, then I'm going to criticize you.’"

Sydney Thomas mocked LSU head coach Lane Kiffin before Halloween with a joke about dressing up as him losing to Ole Miss. The costume idea, for whatever reason, ended up not making the cut this year.

Maybe she couldn’t figure out how to work boobs into the whole look. I don't know, that's purely speculation on my part. And before you laugh, with the costume she chose, she managed to make them part of it.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

Sydney Thomas attends the 61st Academy of Country Music Awards at MGM Grand Garden Arena in Las Vegas, Nev., on May 17, 2026. (Denise Truscello/WireImage)

Sydney went a step further with her Erling Haaland-inspired look. She reminded us that putting boobs on someone is truly one of the best ways to pay tribute to them. Again, don't laugh. Not yet, anyway, you haven’t seen what I'm talking about.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Sydney Thomas arrives at EA Sports presents The Madden Bowl at Orpheum Theater in New Orleans, Louisiana, on Feb. 7, 2025. (Kaitlyn Morris/Getty Images)

A few days ago, the internet's favorite ring girl shared her Halloween costume on Instagram with a carousel of pictures and a "Haappy Haaloween" caption. She tagged the Norwegian soccer star in the post.

One of the images, the fourth one in the carousel for the impatient ones out there, is a face-swap type one, thanks to the power of AI. It put Haaland's head on Thomas' body while in her Halloween costume.

PAUL SKENES AND LIVVY DUNNE'S HALLOWEEN COSTUME WILL ENRAGE ANYONE TIRED OF RUSHING THROUGH HOLIDAYS

Some, I fear, missed the point here. They mistook a touching tribute to the World Cup star as something to be terrified of. I don't believe that's the intent.

Sydney Thomas was having some fun with it, is all. Those make for some of the best costumes. They also make for some of the best tributes you're going to find.

OUTKICK IS NOW ON THE FOX APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

Sydney Thomas attends Lionsgate's Los Angeles premiere of "The Housemaid" at TCL Chinese Theatre on Dec. 15, 2025, in Los Angeles, Calif. (Getty Images for Lionsgate)

Without question, the Lane Kiffin costume would have been good. The Erling Haaland costume, however, and the tribute that it includes is great.

It checks several boxes. Arguably the most important box it checks is the tribute box. It's never too late to go viral with your Halloween costume.

title: Aldi rolls out more than 30 holiday items under $10 with new drops every Wednesday in November

German supermarket chain Aldi is decking its aisles with new seasonal it...
body_text:
The German supermarket chain Aldi's is releasing new limited-time items every Wednesday through Nov. 25, all priced under $10.

German supermarket chain Aldi is decking its aisles with new seasonal items throughout November as the store helps shoppers get in the holiday spirit.

Every Wednesday until Nov. 25, the grocery chain will roll out limited-time festive products including frozen snacks and appetizers, sweet treats and more, according to Food & Wine.

In keeping with the chain’s reputation for affordability, the more than 30 new items will all cost less than $10.

TARGET UNVEILS $30 THANKSGIVING DINNER DEAL AS RETAILERS BATTLE TO OFFER LOWEST PRICES

Fox News Digital reached out to Aldi, headquartered in Batavia, Illinois, for comment.

Aldi’s popular Advent calendars returned on Nov. 4 as part of the first weekly item drop of the month.

Supermarket chain Aldi is introducing over 30 seasonal items throughout November with weekly drops on Wednesdays. (iStock)

Along with the classic chocolate-filled calendars, others contain cheese, wine, beer, tea, beauty products and more.

There are even Advent calendars for dogs.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Other festive finds released on Nov. 4 included crab cakes and lobster cakes, iced gingerbread cookies and pigs in a blanket wrapped in pastry dough with everything bagel seasoning.

The Nov. 11 lineup will include items like peppermint mocha and caramel brûlée-flavored ground coffee, dark chocolate-covered cranberries, sugar cookie kettle corn and a maple nut brioche loaf, Food & Wine reported.

Aldi offers a wide variety of Advent calendars, extending beyond the traditional chocolate-filled version. (iStock)

Other products coming this month include pot roast pastry bites filled with beef and Swiss cheese, chicken nuggets shaped like Christmas trees, candy canes and stockings, and chocolate peppermint bark.

This month’s holiday items arrive in the wake of the many Thanksgiving products that hit stores in October, including a sweet potato casserole, cranberry jalapeño dip, truffle cheddar cheese, scalloped potatoes and more.

Seasonal finds at Aldi tend to generate buzz online, with fans discussing their favorite items they secured at the grocery chain during the holidays.

"Stumbled upon these two sets of pjs in my size for $2.50 each! Also, this cookie jar that I’ve had my eye on since they put it out was marked down to $5.50," one Reddit user wrote last holiday season.

Aldi's seasonal items include multiple frozen snacks and appetizers, including pot roast puff pastry bites and pigs in a blanket. (Aldi)

"There were other great deals and markdowns of pretty much all the holiday stuff," the person added.

Another individual mentioned a crafting Advent calendar that included supplies to make sand art, bracelets and other projects.

"Overall worth the purchase," the person wrote.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

A similar product, the "Creativity For Kids Sensory Play Advent Calendar," is available at Aldi this holiday season.

Aldi has more than 2,000 stores across 36 states, according to the company’s corporate website.

It also noted the chain has been named "the Best Value among U.S. grocery stores."

title: Independent wrestling's heart still beating even as social media begins to write its obituary
excerpt:
Pro wrestler Ben Bishop talks to OutKick about whether he believes independent wrestling is dying.

The pro wrestling conversation on social media usually ranges from hotly contested debates between w...
body_text:
Pro wrestler Ben Bishop talks to OutKick about whether he believes independent wrestling is dying.

The pro wrestling conversation on social media usually ranges from hotly contested debates between which company is better, WWE or AEW, fans complaining about the way their favorite wrestler is booked or there being too many commercials on TV. OK, maybe the last one is just me tweeting into the void.

Regardless, there was a lot of chatter online about independent wrestling being "dead." The noise around the notion appeared to spark when Produce Wrestling and Absolute Intense Wrestling (AIW) announced hiatuses for different reasons for the end of the year. For what it’s worth, Produce already has a show booked for Feb. 25.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

Ben Bishop enters the ring at Fight Factory Wrestling's No Thanks Given on Nov. 6, 2026. (OutKick)

OutKick Dropkick has put the spotlight on several independent shows this year with a few different promotions, including Pandemonium Pro Wrestling, Awesome Championship Wrestling, Produce Wrestling, Gamechanger Wrestling, Fight Factory Wrestling and others. So, as social media wrote an obituary for the indies, OutKick Dropkick made its way to Middletown, New Jersey, on Friday night to take in Fight Factory’s No Thanks Given and to see whether the vibes would be more of a concert or a wake. It didn’t disappoint.

Ben Bishop, who made a surprise appearance at Total Nonstop Action Wrestling’s (TNA) Bound for Glory pay-per-view assembled a team for an elimination eight-person tag team match against MADE. Richard Holliday, Jack Vaughn and Madisyn Maxwell went up against Made. Kristin Blaze then defeated Rachel Ley in a preview of what women’s wrestling may look like in the future. Even WWE Hall of Famer Arn Anderson showed up to support his sons as they took on Sent 2 Salute.

The main event featured a no holds barred match between TNA star KC Navarro and Steve Gibki for the latter’s openweight championship. The match ended with Gibki spearing Navarro through a table and putting his opponent in the Hell Hammer for the win.

The show was held at the Middletown Sports Complex, which is not a large venue by any means. But pro wrestling fans still showed up to fill the available seats. Most lasted through the chilly conditions since the event took place on a literal ice rink, which is also the home of the North American Hockey League’s New Jersey Titans.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Richard Holliday appears at Fight Factory Wrestling's No Thanks Given on Nov. 6, 2026. (OutKick)

There certainly was no funeral for independent wrestling. In fact, attendees were actively engaged in the sport that was happening in and outside of the ring.

OutKick Dropkick asked Bishop whether he believed the indies were dead.

"I mean, look at it, look at it here. In Middletown, New Jersey, on a Friday night, you could be doing anything," Bishop said. "We're close to (New York City). There's a ton of things you can do. We got about 300, almost 400-plus here in Middletown, New Jersey, here at Fight Factory. You can thank me for the house. So yeah, this whole notion, indies are dead, all that stuff, it's just words, it's just noise. It comes up every few months. Everyone wants to pretend that they think that when they were wrestling on the indies, it was so much better. It is what it is. Things evolve, things change. I believe that indie wrestling is alive and well."

Anyone who was in the facility on Friday night could have been doing anything else. WWE’s "Friday Night SmackDown" was on TV, "World of Warcraft’s" new game just dropped, there was basketball and hockey going on at the same time.

And maybe you don’t know who Ben Bishop is. Maybe you didn’t see his "curtain call" with Holliday, Vaughn and Tommy Invincible at War on the Shore 3 that had social media talking over the summer. And all of that is OK.

OutKick Dropkick asked Killer Kross his thoughts about the same notion. Kross works for a big-time company in Major League Wrestling, which has multiple media rights deals and partnerships with CMLL and New Japan Pro-Wrestling. However, he’s gone on his own tours in the U.S. and abroad for promotions big and small.

Kross said he wasn’t necessarily plugged into the conversation but suggested that the attendance at independent events undercut the notion that independent wrestling is dying.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"No, that's hilarious to me," he said. "These are people who don't attend indies that are saying that, and I don't even think they're saying it to be malicious. I think they're just innocently saying it because You know, when, when you're a young adult and you have a very busy life, if you're not paying attention to something, or like you're not paying attention to the big main thing that everybody's paying attention to, then you innocently will think that it's not important cause it doesn't have your attention.

"But when you go to an independent show where there's 2,000-3000 people there, That kind of speaks for itself. I don't get involved with neurotic conversations online. You know what I mean? And it's OK. Anyone can express their opinion about anything they want. I don't get hung up on that, but like … I don't know, I'm not emotionally prone to these types of conversations. Some people are like, ‘Well, I gotta drop everything I'm doing and respond.’ I'm like, I don't have the time. I don't have the time."

Pro wrestlers who aren’t exclusively signed to the major corporate companies are working their tails off to make a living in their sport and to put on a good show for those who do come out and see them.

Not every venue is going to be Allegiant Stadium or Wembley Stadium. The pro wrestlers who work these shows know that and work together to put on the best matches they can to keep the fans coming back for more.

Is independent wrestling dying? No chance.

Alanis Morissette’s recent decision to publicly identify as pansexual has cast her famous same-sex kiss with Sarah Jessica Parker on "Sex and the City" in a new light.

The singer, 52, opened up about her sexuality during an appearance on the "Handsome" podcast after previously discussing the memorable 2000 scene on Alex Cooper’s "Call Her Daddy" podcast in September.

Morissette appeared on "Sex and the City" in the season 3 episode "Boy, Girl, Boy, Girl…" as Dawn, a woman who kisses Parker’s character, Carrie Bradshaw, during a game of spin the bottle.

During her September appearance on "Call Her Daddy," Morissette revealed that she helped pitch the storyline to the show’s producers.

"I reached out to them and I said, ‘Might it be a nice time for Carrie to experience a lesbian moment?’" Morissette said. "And they said, ‘Why, yes. We were thinking the same thing.’"

Alanis Morissette’s 1995 album topped the Billboard 200, earned multiple Grammy Awards and helped cement her status as a music icon. (Jamie McCarthy/Getty Images)

Morissette also reflected on the kiss itself, describing the moment with Parker as "easy" and "buoyant."

"I do recall kissing her," she said. "It was very pleasant."

"I’ve felt love from the gay community since I was really young because all my friends were gay," Morissette added. "There’s a passion, a presence, and a curiosity with a lot of gay people that I meet, and that aliveness is such a special quality to me."

title: ‘Seismic shift’: Native American women made significant gains in US midterms
excerpt:
Nationwide, voters elected at least 75 Native women or non-binary candidates in Tuesday’s elections, report says

The US midterm elections saw voters elect a slew of historic representatives – from th...
body_text:
Nationwide, voters elected at least 75 Native women or non-binary candidates in Tuesday’s elections, report says

The US midterm elections saw voters elect a slew of historic representatives – from the country’s first Muslim senator to the first Black female governor – but among the most significant gains were those for Native American women.

On Tuesday, voters elected the first Native American woman governor, senator and leaders of two tribal nations. Nationwide, voters elected at least 75 Native women or non-binary and Two Spirit candidates in the November midterms, according to Advance Native Political Leadership and the news site ICT.

Deb Haaland, a citizen of Laguna Pueblo and Joe Biden’s former interior secretary, will lead the state of New Mexico. Peggy Flanagan, a member of the White Earth band of Ojibwe and current Minnesota lt governor, will represent her state in the US Senate. Crystalyne Curley will become the first woman to lead the Navajo Nation, one of the country’s largest tribes. And Tina Abrams will lead the Seneca Nation of Indians in western New York, also the first woman leader in the modern history of the state’s largest tribe.

Mary Peltola, who is Yup’ik, could join Flanagan as another first Native woman in the US Senate pending the results of her still undecided race in Alaska.

“This is a seismic shift that is happening in our communities,” Jordan James Harvill, a citizen of the Cherokee Nation and strategist with Advance Native Political Leadership, told the Associated Press.

Although Native Americans have made significant gains in political power in recent years, it has been a long road to get here. Native Americans have only been allowed to vote across the entire United States since the 1960s. In 1985, Wilma Mankiller became the first woman elected to serve as principal chief of the Cherokee Nation.

In 2018, Haaland and Sharice Davids, a member of the Ho-Chunk Nation, became the first women elected to Congress when they both won seats in the House of Representatives alongside a wave of progressive freshmen lawmakers, including Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Ilhan Omar and Rashida Tlaib. Davids was easily re-elected last week in Kansas to a fifth term in Congress.

“The first thing that made [running for office] feel really possible was seeing Deb Haaland, was seeing Sharice Davids on a national level,” New Mexico state senator Angel Charley, who is Laguna/Zuni/Diné, told the Guardian about her decision to enter state politics in 2024.

In 2020, after an outpouring of voters from the Navajo and Hopi reservations in Arizona saw the long-red state vote for Biden, he named Haaland to lead the interior department, making her the first Indigenous cabinet secretary.

The same year, Yvette Herrell, who is Cherokee, became the first Republican Native woman elected to Congress. She served from 2021 to 2023.

This election cycle, a record-setting 363 Indigenous candidates ran for office in local, state and federal elections across the country – with at least 180 of them winning their races. Among them were Claire Valdez, a citizen of Ysleta del Sur Pueblo and Democrat from New York, who will join Davids in the US House of Representatives.

The Senate has seen four Native men represent their states in its 237 year history, but Flanagan will be the first Native woman to join the chamber in January.

At her victory party in St Paul, Minnesota, Flanagan told supporters: “I could not run for the US Senate without Native women. I could not exist in the way that I do without Native women.”

For Haaland, the historic nature of the election isn’t lost on her – but in the final weeks of a hectic campaign she told the Guardian that she sometimes forgets she’s on the verge of a milestone.

“Sometimes I forget about the fact that I would be the first Native woman. We’re in the throes of this statewide campaign and it’s so busy and we’re trying to be everywhere all at once,” she said in a recent interview. “But I recognize that for some people who feel like they haven’t ever been represented – I really, I’m grateful that I have this opportunity … I just hope that I can help folks to see that hard work still means something. That anyone can be a leader regardless of where you come from or how much money you do or don’t have.”

In 2023, New Mexico became the first and only state in the country to implement an updated Native American Voting Rights Act, which gave tribes greater input on polling locations and redistricting.

For the Navajo Nation, the largest tribal nation by geography – spanning approximately 27,000 sq miles across parts of New Mexico, Arizona and Utah – Curley’s victory in tribal elections also held on Tuesday was significant. Curley is currently the speaker of the Navajo Nation council and became the first woman to hold that position in 2022.

“As women, we have to work twice or triple as hard, especially within Navajo politics,” she told the AP, adding that she faced sexist rhetoric during her campaign. “This is a win for all Navajo women.”

“I am humbled,” Abrams, the Seneca Nation’s president-elect said in a statement after her victory. “Tonight, at long last, a woman will now lead our Nation as president. This is a moment inspired by generations of strong Seneca women who came before me, and one that I hope inspires generations of Seneca women who come after me.”
